title: refactor(app-shell): Explain access picks its object and operation with the shared Select (objectui#11865)
body:
Part of #11865
Clause-②: no

The *Explain access* slice of objectui#11865 (claim 6063378622): the panel's two browser-native select elements, *Object* and *Operation*, become the shared Radix `Select`. The card stays open for the other native selects its body counts. The earlier slices are objectui#11934 (the Group panel) and objectui#11976 (the validation editor).

## What changed

- `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/AccessExplainPanel.tsx`: one module-private `ExplainPicker`, drawn with the shared `Select` from `@object-ui/components`, renders both pickers. It follows the validation editor's `RulePicker`: items carry their option's index, so "Select an object…" (value `''`, which `SelectItem` refuses) needs no stand-in value, and a value none of the options carries gets an item of its own. The trigger carries the control's `id`, so each label's `htmlFor` still names it.
- Untouched: the free-text `Input` fallback when the package lists no objects, the user picker, the record selector, the explain request, the props and the exports. No i18n key is added; the panel's set of `engine.*` keys is identical to the base's (diffed).
- `AccessExplainPanel.sharedSelect-11865.test.tsx` (new), and `AccessExplainPanel.test.tsx`, whose package-scoped dropdown test now opens and picks through the trigger. It still checks the same three things: the options listed, the free-text placeholder gone, and the object the request sends.
- `.changeset/11865-explain-access-shared-select.md`: `@object-ui/app-shell: patch`.

## Why Select and not Combobox for the object list

Triage allows `Combobox` where a list is long, and a package's object list is open-ended, so it was built first and measured. Both readings come from Chromium, on a scratch page that mounted this panel with a package of 25 objects. The scratch page was deleted and never committed.

- **Shared `Combobox`** (built, then kept out of the branch): a 400 px mouse wheel over its open list left `scrollTop` at 0, with the list's `scrollHeight` 840 and `clientHeight` 300. The panel lives in a `Sheet`, and there the list did not scroll under the wheel.
- **Shared `Select`**: the same wheel moved its viewport from 0 to 208, the maximum for `scrollHeight` 840 and `clientHeight` 632. Typing `showcase_t` in the open list jumped to `showcase_task`.

The `Combobox` also reports a re-pick of its current option as `''`. So the object list is a `Select`, like the operation list.

## Dispatch hypotheses

- **H1, value parity: held.** The base panel was read first with a scratch probe (not committed): a `change` on each native option, then Explain. The new suite pins every option of both pickers against the request body read there:
  - each object sends its name;
  - each of the seven operations sends its name;
  - "Select an object…" leaves Explain disabled, as on the base;
  - re-picking the current option sends the same request.

  One caveat: the probe's `change` event fires even for the current option, so the re-pick rows pin the primitive's behaviour, not a browser reading of the native one.
- **H2, labels and keyboard: held.**
  - `getByRole('combobox', { name: 'Object' })` and `{ name: 'Operation' }` find the two triggers (the base probe found the native controls by the same names).
  - Enter opens each picker and Enter on an option selects it. This is pinned in the test DOM and was also seen in Chromium.
  - The panel has no disabled or read-only state. It takes no such prop, its one mount (`StudioDesignSurface`) passes `open`, `onOpenChange` and `packageId`, and it writes no metadata. So objectui#11781 has nothing to reach here.
- **H3, a value outside the options: held.**
  - On the base, a held object the package does not list (`crm_lead`) showed "Select an object…" (`selectedIndex` 0), while Explain sent `crm_lead`.
  - Now the trigger shows `crm_lead`, and it is listed first. Picking it changes nothing, and Explain still sends `crm_lead`.
  - The pin reaches that state through `defaultObject`.
- **H4, first-load bytes: measured, −1 gzip byte.**
  - Method: `apps/console` `vite build`, then `node scripts/check-eager-closure-budget.mjs`, on this head and on the same tree with the panel at its base blob `5aade6a7`, the only bundle input the branch changes.
  - Eager gzip bytes: 3390584 on head and 3390585 on base. Eager raw bytes are equal (11491936), with the same 337 of 2459 eager chunks.
  - The only eager chunk that moves is the entry `index` chunk: 0 raw bytes, −1 gzip byte.
  - The panel ships in the lazy `studioBuilder` chunk on both legs.
  - The gate prints the same line on both legs: "Console eager closure is 3311.1 KB gzipped across 337 of 2459 chunks (budget: 3312.0 KB, headroom: 0.9 KB)".
  - These are local builds. The budget bot's reading on this PR is the one that counts.

## Tests and gates, on head `0c5300d7c`

- Repo-root `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2` over the new suite, `AccessExplainPanel.test.tsx` and `AccessExplainPanel.principalPerson-11862.test.tsx`, the only suites that mount the real panel (the `StudioDesignSurface` suites stub it): "Test Files 3 passed (3)", "Tests 28 passed (28)".
- The two repo-wide pins, `packages/core/src/utils/__tests__/column-identity.ratchet.test.ts` and `scripts/__tests__/one-authority-per-exported-name-6273.test.ts`: "Test Files 2 passed (2)", "Tests 18 passed (18)".
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` (echoes `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`) exits 0. It ran after the `@object-ui/app-shell^...` closure build (29 projects, exit 0). `--listFilesOnly` shows the panel in the main program and all three panel suites in the test program.
- `pnpm exec eslint` on the three touched files exits 0. The JSON format reports 3 files, 0 errors and 8 warnings. The base blobs of the two existing files report the same 8 (`no-explicit-any` and `set-state-in-effect` in untouched code), and the new suite reports none.
- All exit 0:
  - `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` ("3 source file(s) of 1 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s)");
  - `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`;
  - `pnpm check:new-line-citations` ("0 new citation(s)");
  - `pnpm check:control-bytes`;
  - `check-changeset-fixed`, `check-changeset-overwrite`, `check-changeset-claims`;
  - `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:test-path-roots`;
  - `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`;
  - `check:phantom-deps`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:i18n-keys`, `check:i18n-designer-parity`, `check:metadata-write-doors`.
- Declared to CI: the full `pnpm test` farm and repo-wide `pnpm lint`.

**Reverse leg.** The implementation was committed first (`a551c491f`). The panel was then written from its base blob, and the landing was proven: 2 native select elements, 0 `ExplainPicker`, and a hash equal to the base blob. The new suite and `AccessExplainPanel.test.tsx` then read "Tests 18 failed | 5 passed (23)":

- red: all 17 new pins, and the package-scoped dropdown test;
- green: the other five existing tests.

That is the direction the suite header predicts. The trap restored the file with `git checkout HEAD --`. The restore was proven: the hash equals the HEAD blob and `git diff HEAD` is 0 bytes.

## Acceptance notes

- **The shared `Combobox` inside a `Sheet`.** Its open list did not scroll under the mouse wheel, measured once in Chromium on the scratch page above. This bears on this card's own remaining work: a later slice that moves a long list inside a dialog or sheet to `Combobox` would meet it. It is not filed from here, because no public entry on `main` was measured. `ObjectRefField` and `RecipientPickerField` import the `Combobox`, and whether either one renders inside a modal was not read.
- **The `Combobox`'s search reads the option value only.** It passes no keywords to cmdk, so an option's label (a translated object label, for example) is not searchable. This was read from source and not measured.
- **`defaultObject` has no caller in the tree.** In the tree, the outside-the-options state is reached by text typed into the free-text input before the package's object list arrives (read from source, not measured).
